questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a natural join?

options.text: A join that combines all columns from two tables without any condition.
A join that combines rows with matching values in specified columns.
A join that automatically matches columns with the same name and removes duplicates.
A join that combines all rows from two tables, regardless of matching.

questions.explanation: A natural join automatically matches columns with the same name in both tables and removes duplicate columns, which distinguishes it from other types of joins.

questions.stem: What is the result of a left outer join between two tables $R$ and $S$?

options.text: Only the rows where there is a match in both tables.
All rows from $R$, and matched rows from $S$.
All rows from $S$, and matched rows from $R$.
All rows from both $R$ and $S$, regardless of matching.

questions.explanation: A left outer join returns all rows from the left table $R$, and the matched rows from the right table $S$. Unmatched rows from $R$ will have NULLs for columns from $S$.

questions.stem: If a table $R$ has 8 rows and a table $S$ has 3 rows, what is the maximum number of rows in the Cartesian product $R \times S$?
questions.explanation: The Cartesian product $R \times S$ results in $|R| \times |S|$ rows. With $|R| = 8$ and $|S| = 3$, the product has $8 \times 3 = 24$ rows.

questions.stem: Calculate the number of rows in the result of a full outer join between tables $R$ with 15 rows and $S$ with 10 rows, assuming 5 rows match. Provide your answer as a whole number.
questions.explanation: In a full outer join, all rows from both tables are included. The total number of rows is the sum of unmatched rows from $R$ and $S$, plus the matched rows. Here, $15 + 10 - 5 = 20$ rows.
